topicName: Model Serving with TorchServe and Triton
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Model Serving with TorchServe and Triton in PyTorch"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Deploying PyTorch models to production requires robust serving frameworks that can handle concurrent requests, dynamic batching, and GPU acceleration. Two of the most popular solutions are TorchServe, the official PyTorch-native serving engine, and NVIDIA Triton Inference Server, a highly optimized multi-framework serving engine. This tutorial covers how to package and serve PyTorch models using both solutions."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Model Serving with TorchServe"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"TorchServe uses a packaged archive format called '.mar' (Model Archive) which bundles the model weights, the model architecture, and a custom handler script that defines preprocessing, inference, and postprocessing steps."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from ts.torch_handler.base_handler import BaseHandler

class MNISTHandler(BaseHandler):
    def __init__(self):
        super(MNISTHandler, self).__init__()
        self.model = None

    def preprocess(self, data):
        # Convert incoming payload to tensor
        payload = data[0].get('data') or data[0].get('body')
        tensor = torch.tensor(payload['image'], dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(0)
        return tensor

    def inference(self, model_input):
        with torch.no_grad():
            return self.model(model_input)

    def postprocess(self, inference_output):
        predictions = torch.argmax(inference_output, dim=1).tolist()
        return [{'prediction': predictions[0]}]"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"To package the model, use the 'torch-model-archiver' CLI tool. This command packages the serialized weights, model definition, and custom handler into a single '.mar' file:"},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"torch-model-archiver --model-name mnist_model --version 1.0 --model-file model.py --serialized-file weights.pt --handler custom_handler.py --export-path model_store"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Start the TorchServe server pointing to your model store directory:"},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"torchserve --start --model-store model_store --models mnist=mnist_model.mar"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Model Serving with NVIDIA Triton"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"NVIDIA Triton Inference Server is designed for high-throughput, low-latency serving. It requires a specific directory structure called a Model Repository and a configuration file named 'config.pbtxt'. Triton natively supports TorchScript, ONNX, and TensorRT backends."},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"First, export your PyTorch model to TorchScript format:"},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torchvision.models as models

model = models.resnet50(pretrained=True)
model.eval()

# Trace the model with a dummy input
dummy_input = torch.rand(1, 3, 224, 224)
traced_model = torch.jit.trace(model, dummy_input)
traced_model.save('model.pt')"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Next, organize your model repository directory structure as follows:

model_repository/
└── resnet50/
    ├── config.pbtxt
    └── 1/
        └── model.pt"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Define the 'config.pbtxt' file to specify the backend, input/output tensor shapes, and data types:"},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"name: "resnet50"
platform: "pytorch_libtorch"
max_batch_size: 8
input [
  {
    name: "input__0"
    data_type: TYPE_FP32
    dims: [ 3, 224, 224 ]
  }
]
output [
  {
    name: "output__0"
    data_type: TYPE_FP32
    dims: [ 1000 ]
  }
]"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Run the Triton server using Docker, mounting your model repository directory:"},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"docker run --gpus=all --rm -p 8000:8000 -p 8001:8001 -p 8002:8002 -v /path/to/model_repository:/models nvcr.io/nvidia/tritonserver:23.05-py3 tritonserver --model-repository=/models"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Comparing TorchServe and Triton"},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"TorchServe is PyTorch-native, making it easier to write custom Python preprocessing and postprocessing handlers directly without exporting to intermediate formats."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Triton offers superior performance with advanced features like dynamic batching, concurrent model execution, and shared memory support."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Triton supports multiple frameworks (TensorFlow, ONNX, TensorRT, PyTorch) simultaneously, whereas TorchServe is specialized for PyTorch."},{"order":23,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"Choose TorchServe if you want a quick, Python-centric deployment path with minimal format conversion. Choose Triton Inference Server if you require ultra-low latency, high throughput, dynamic batching, or need to serve models from multiple deep learning frameworks on the same hardware."}]
